title: Monday · Reconciliation Walk, decimals and Nevermoor
arrival: Our Reconciliation Walk begins at 9:30. Start with your teacher's morning directions.
note: Working plan. Walk return may shift; outdoor choice time expands or contracts with it. Carry math practice forward if reconciliation learning needs more time. Career content stays flexible until the Be The Change Earth Alliance resource is reviewed. LST timing awaits final confirmation. Planned teaching, not a completion record.

blocks.title: Social Studies · TRC Calls to Action
blocks.notes: Connect Orange Shirt Day and previous residential school learning to the TRC's purpose: Survivors and communities called for changes, not just awareness. Select one education-related Call to Action from NCTR (for example, #62 about education developed with Indigenous peoples) and attribute it. Brief sequence: recall learning; read and paraphrase the selected call; ask who is asked to act, what should change and why; invite one spoken or written response. Finish before walk preparation. Source: https://nctr.ca/about/truth-and-reconciliation-commission-of-canada-calls-to-action/
studentSteps: What change does this Call to Action ask for?
Who needs to act, and why does it matter?

blocks.title: Get ready for the walk
blocks.notes: Washroom, outdoor clothing, route and group expectations. Check the accessible route and participation choices with support staff; leave 9:25–9:30 for transition to the starting point.

blocks.title: Reconciliation Walk
blocks.notes: Expected walk is about 20–30 minutes, with return around 9:50–10:00. Follow school guidance for route and gathering point.

blocks.title: Outdoor community choices
blocks.notes: Use remaining time for inclusive, accessible choice-based play and connection, not a formal PE lesson. Offer usable pavement space and choices such as chalk, casual ball passing, walking and talking or an accessible game students choose together. Check that each student can participate meaningfully. Expand or shorten according to return time.
studentSteps: Choose a way to move, play or talk together.
Make room for everyone to join in.

blocks.title: Snack
blocks.notes: Return, wash hands and have snack before recess. Timing can flex slightly with the walk.

blocks.title: Mathematics · compare and round decimals
blocks.notes: Model aligned-digit comparison: 4.386 > 4.368 because the hundredths digits differ (8 > 6). Round 4.386 to the nearest hundredth: the thousandths digit 6 rounds the hundredths 8 up to 9, giving 4.39. Guide a second example together. Independent check: compare 4.305 and 4.350 (4.305 < 4.350); round 7.264 to the nearest hundredth (7.26). Ask students to explain the deciding digit. Use existing decimal resources if helpful; carry remaining practice forward if morning timing shifts.
studentSteps: Compare decimals one place at a time.
Try the short check on your own.

blocks.title: Quiet individual time
blocks.notes: Independent reading, drawing or appropriate colouring. A calm return from lunch.

blocks.title: Language Arts · Nevermoor
blocks.notes: Resume listening from the class's actual stopping point; do not guess a chapter. Pause for one character choice and a supporting detail. Model a two-sentence response, then ask students for one brief written, drawn-with-caption or spoken response using a detail from today's listening. No large assignment.
studentSteps: Share a short response with a story detail.

blocks.title: Career Education · strengths and contribution
blocks.notes: Flexible launch while the existing Be The Change Earth Alliance Career resource awaits review. Use a simple discussion or note: name one strength or interest, one value or community need, and one way people can contribute. Link gently to future careers, responsibility and possible solutions; do not imply the booklet has been selected or copy its contents. See the Career Education curriculum planning placeholder.
studentSteps: Name a strength or interest you can use.
How could it help someone or our community?

blocks.title: Classroom community
blocks.notes: Flexible reflection, community-building or unfinished learning. A short check-in about including everyone outdoors can fit if useful.

blocks.title: Planners, jobs and dismissal
blocks.notes: Planners, classroom jobs, cleanup and dismissal preparation.
